audit.why: 46.73% over 107 games. Infected Bonesaw is 975 range on a 4-second cooldown against a 900-range Q on 9 seconds, so Mundo out-ranges and out-cycles Aurora's poke outright — the Mundo-sided 2-3 and both item stages are right, and Aurora's only real windows are level 1 and the 4-6 stretch before Maximum Dosage.

audit.whatIsWrong: The Level 6 phase named her ultimate "Between the Worlds" and said nothing about what Maximum Dosage does to the 6 spike, which is the whole story of this lane.
audit.why: Maximum Dosage is a flat 120s at every rank and 'instantly heals a percent of his missing Health', then regenerates a portion of max health over a long duration. It rewards him for being low, which is exactly the state your poke pattern puts him in. Between Worlds is 140s, so he gets his back 20 seconds sooner and the trade is worse for you at every rank.
audit.corrected: Between Worlds (R, 140s) zones his all-in, but Maximum Dosage is a flat 120s and heals off missing health — poking him low feeds it.

audit.whatIsWrong: Three content fields (spikes[2].text, wants.you[1], mid) plus whys[4] say Between Worlds makes Aurora untargetable so his cleaver and E 'whiff entirely'. Aurora has no untargetability. Meanwhile the one interaction that genuinely decides this lane — how Heart Zapper's heal is denied — is stated nowhere, and Goes Where He Pleases is absent from both layers.
audit.why: Heart Zapper (W, 17/16.5/16/15.5/15, 325 range): 'stores a portion of damage he takes. At the end of the duration or on Recast, Dr. Mundo deals a burst of damage to nearby enemies. If the burst hit an enemy, he heals a percentage of the stored damage.' The heal is conditional on the burst connecting — so being more than 325 units away when it detonates denies the entire heal, no Grievous Wounds required. That is a free, repeatable counterplay and it is worth more than any item in this matchup. Goes Where He Pleases (P) 'resists the first Immobilizing effect that hits him', which is what breaks jungle ganks on him and why setting one up needs two sources of CC, not one. Blunt Force Trauma (E) deals 'additional damage based on his missing Health', so he gets more dangerous exactly as your poke works — and it is an auto-attack reset, so his wind-up is the tell. Infected Bonesaw (Q) scales on your current health, so it hits hardest when you are full.
audit.corrected: Heart Zapper only heals him if its burst hits you — step outside 325 units before it detonates and he heals nothing.

audit.whatIsWrong: Heart Zapper is tracked without its number, and the page tells you to fight 'on his Q cooldown' — Infected Bonesaw is 4 seconds and never meaningfully down.
audit.why: Heart Zapper at 17s is the only cooldown in his kit long enough to plan around. Infected Bonesaw at 4s and Blunt Force Trauma at 9s both return faster than you can reposition.
audit.corrected: Heart Zapper is 17s — the only window. His cleaver is 4s and never down.

audit.whatIsWrong: No mention that his passive blanks the first crowd control in a gank.
audit.why: A jungler arriving with one immobilizing spell gets it eaten by Goes Where He Pleases and the gank fails. Two CC sources, or a cannister he cannot walk over, is the requirement.
audit.corrected: Goes Where He Pleases eats the first immobilize — a one-CC gank on Mundo does nothing.

notes: The single most useful unwritten fact in this matchup is that Heart Zapper's heal is conditional on its burst connecting — walking out of 325 units denies it entirely, which is stronger and cheaper than the anti-heal the page leads with. Infected Bonesaw at 975 range also out-ranges Twofold Hex at 900, so the page's framing of Aurora as the poke winner is wrong in the range war; the recorded Mundo-sided level 2-3 already reflects the outcome. The 'mid' paragraph still carries the untargetability claim and still tells the player to fight on his 4-second cleaver cooldown; both need a rewrite that did not fit the length band here.
